newsitem.title: UK: Handy-size demand seen in quiet freight market.
newsitem.headline: Handy-size demand seen in quiet freight market.

text.p: Brokers were reluctant to express views about the immediate course of the dry cargo freight market during a quiet opening to the week.
For once handy-sizes appeared to be in good demand, particularly from USGulf and the plate. Caper trading was largely featureless.

Brokers said there was steady interest in Panamaxes generally but marginally lower rates had been fixed in some trades. A number of vessels were booked for period business in the East. The BFI shed 5 points to 1442.

GRAIN - Active chartering of tonnage for grain to Iran and Saudi Arabia was reported by brokers today although few details of rates were available. Iranians were believed to have covered business from the Plate with trade Greece 54,615 dwt and Horizon a 64,619 dwt to Bandar Abbas or Bandar Khomeini.

Michele Iuliano 64,850 dwt was linked with Iris l for an end Dec stem of 60,000/5 wheat Canadian Pacific/Iraat $20.25. Toepfer and Dreyfus were rumoured to have both taken Panamax tonnage for grain business from Nopac to Saudi Arabia, but further information was lacking. Glencore were believed to be quoting a December stem on this route.

In the Atlantic Oinoussian Sky 64,377 dwt was said to be working Romac for grain to Egypt, Anangel Argonaut 65,668 dwt was believed taken on subjects in the Med, and Dreyfus rumoured fixed 55,000 heavy grain St Lawrence/Continent at $9.85.
Reports of stronger demand for tonnage from the Plate was a feature of today's market.

Following news last week that Pioneer relet Ascona 64,942 dwt for grain business to Denmark on private business it was learned that Marifran fixed Eleni 73,040 dwt delivery spot French Bay for 2 laden legs Atlantic business via East Coast South America at $11,000 daily.

Interest in Handy-size tonnage appeared to be building up with new enquiries quoted, for example, by Andre for 23,000 wheat Up River/Port Dan for Dec 6/15 and Jebsen for a vessel of 26/32,000 dwt delivery Plate Nov 30/Dec 10 trip Buenaventura.

Other new business for Handies included Cargill for 30,000 heavy grain Baie Comeau/Lisbon for Dec 10/15 and NSAC for 37,000/42,000 dwt delivery NOPAC Dec 16/23 trip Singapore-Japan range. Garnac was said to have covered 20,000 heavy grain prompt US Gulf/Puerto Cabello and 13,000 tonnes St Lawrence/Puerto Cabello for Dec 2/10 on private terms.

MINERALS - The Caper market continued dormant, but a number of Panamaxes went for period business with far East delivery. Success Bulker 64,120 dwt was said to have been booked by Navios for 12 months on private terms and Great Chance was said to have continued Rialto 70,677 dwt delivery January for a similar period at about $10,000/10,250 daily.
Hanjin fixed Deerpool 65,163 dwt delivery West Coast Mexico for 4-6 months at close to $10,200 daily plus $80,000 bonus.

HANDY-SIZES - Brokers regarded Bocimar's fixture of Alcestis 43,383 dwt for 2 years delivery far East next month at $8,200 and $8,700 daily for the first and second years respectively as relatively weak.

Pandias 40,907 dwt was rumoured fixed in the East for short period at close to $7,800 daily. On the Continent Van Ommeren fixed Almar for 3-5 months Atlantic trading at $8,000 daily. Arya was booked by Glencore with scrap from the Continent on private terms.
